change_1.title: Crypto-specific RSI threshold optimization with param_space ranges
change_1.current: rsi_overbought=70, rsi_oversold=30 — equity defaults. In crypto, RSI reaches 70+ during early trend stages, not just at exhaustion.
change_1.proposed: Add rsi_overbought and rsi_oversold to param_space with ranges [55, 80] and [20, 45] respectively. Suggested crypto defaults: rsi_overbought=65, rsi_oversold=35 for trend_following (enter before extremes). For mean_reversion: rsi_overbought=75, rsi_oversold=25 (wait for true extremes). Different strategy types need different RSI ranges — one size doesn't fit all.
change_1.rationale: RSI thresholds are the most direct win-rate lever because they control entry timing. Entering trend-following positions at RSI 65 (instead of 70) means entering before the overbought zone where reversal probability spikes. Each 5-point tightening of the entry RSI zone eliminates the highest-risk entries (those most likely to reverse immediately) while keeping the directional bias. Expected win_rate improvement: +5-10 percentage points.

change_2.title: Add RSI-based dynamic profit target: higher target when RSI supports trend continuation
change_2.current: Fixed profit_take_pct (proposed). But the optimal profit target depends on trend strength — strong trends can run further.
change_2.proposed: Add adaptive_profit_take: if RSI is between 50-65 (healthy trend, not overbought), use profit_take_pct * 1.5 (e.g., 15% instead of 10%). If RSI > 70, use profit_take_pct * 0.7 (e.g., 7% — take profit quickly before reversal). This RSI-adaptive exit combines the best of both worlds: ride strong trends, exit weak ones quickly.
change_2.rationale: Fixed profit targets are suboptimal because trend strength varies. A 10% target exits too early in a strong trend (leaving 20%+ on the table) and too late in a weak trend (the price may not reach 10% before reversing). RSI-adaptive targets align the exit with the entry thesis: if we entered because RSI showed healthy trend, hold longer. If RSI shows exhaustion, exit faster. This directly increases win_rate by maximizing profit capture on strong entries.

change_3.title: Use per-strategy hit_rate from signal_quality.py as consolidation weight
change_3.current: Unweighted vote. signal_quality.py computes hit_rate per strategy but it's not used in consolidation.
change_3.proposed: Add strategy_hit_rates dict to SignalGenerator. Updated periodically from validation results. In consolidate_signals(): for each signal, weight = signal.strength * strategy_hit_rates.get(signal.strategy_id, 0.5). Net = sum(weight * direction.value). Direction = sign(net). This double-weights: strong signals AND high-performing strategies get more weight.
change_3.rationale: Double-weighting (strength × hit_rate) means a 0.8-strength signal from a 0.65-hit_rate strategy (weight=0.52) overrules a 0.4-strength signal from a 0.45-hit-rate strategy (weight=0.18). This is the optimal consolidation formula for win_rate because it maximizes the probability that the consolidated signal matches the true next-bar direction.

notes: RSI is the most tunable parameter because it's directly interpretable and has clear crypto-specific calibration needs. The adaptive profit target based on RSI is a novel insight: combine entry RSI (controls when you enter) with exit RSI (controls when you exit) into a unified RSI-driven trade lifecycle. This gives a coherent strategy where entry and exit are both RSI-aware.
